**Issue #2975 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #2975: Patch: a hand card the game won't let you play always says why, and the fuzz holds every card to it
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
When a card in your hand cannot be played, the game says why (not enough mana, no open lane, no legal target). There is a gap. A card that needs a target can have, as its only target, an enemy that costs two discards to target (Paul Allen's Ghost) while you hold too few other cards. That card cannot be played and says nothing, so it simply does nothing when clicked, which is the very bug the explanation was added to fix. Once built, such a card gives its reason, and the random-game checker verifies on every turn that each unplayable hand card has one, so a later rule cannot silently reopen the gap.

## Why
- R979000: `playReason` is on the viewer's hand card while they may act and `legalActions` lists no play of it.
- `crates/engine/src/view_for.rs:684-689` sets it only when `why_hand_card_unplayable` returns a non-empty reason. `why_unplayable` (`crates/engine/src/play_choices.rs:2071-2199`) ends with step (e), which asks only whether the unfiltered `play_choice_combinations(...)` is empty and otherwise returns `None`.
- The listing is narrower: `payable_play_choices` (`play_choices.rs:2423-2438`) drops every combination whose targeting discards cannot be paid (C #89, R682), and R123's tribute agreement (`play_choices.rs:2377`) drops more. Neither is modelled in the reason.
- Only hand-built cases test it (`crates/engine/tests/rules/play_reason.rs`), and no fuzz monitor check reads `playReason`.

## Proposal
- `why_unplayable`'s last step reads the same payable filter and tribute agreement the listing does, and returns that refusal's message (`why_targeting_discards_unpayable`'s) rather than `None`.
- A new fuzz monitor invariant, the next free I-number: while the viewer may act (R979000's window), each own hand card, and each graveyard card a permission lets them play (R1571000), carries `playReason` exactly when the legal list holds no play of it. It reuses the view and legal list I6 already builds (`crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs:2541-2548`), so it costs almost nothing. The tutorial seat's `barred_from_play` is exempted if it needs to be.

## Where it lands
`crates/engine/src/play_choices.rs`, `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs`, `crates/engine/tests/rules/play_reason.rs` (or the tests of `crates/cards/src/scripts/classic/c089_paul_allens_ghost.rs`), the invariant list in `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`'s header; SPEC §10.8.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test named after R979000: a required-target Spell in hand whose only target is an enemy Paul Allen's Ghost, with one other card held, has no listed play and a `playReason` naming the discard. It fails today.
- [ ] A monitor test reports the new invariant on that state before the fix and nothing after.
- [ ] The 200-seed fuzz gate (`cargo jackioh fuzz`) passes with the new check; any further card it finds without a reason gets one.
- [ ] No state, event or replay hash changes (presentation only, CLAUDE.md rule 7); `cargo jackioh golden check` passes.

## Size and risks
Medium: about 4 files, 100 to 150 lines. The new check may turn up other fall-throughs, each needing a reason; that is the point, but it can grow the patch.
```
